text:
Noah: Weird pattern in us-west-2 racks today  seeing NVSwitch/PCIe domain saturation that correlates with tenant spikes, but the heatmap points to cross-socket DMA and not just KV cache misses. 95p token latency +150ms around 2026-04-02 08:12 UTC. :confused:
Priya: Can you dump the hardware counters? NVSwitch vs NVLink vs PCIe DMA would help attribute whether it's intra-board traffic or host DMA.
Noah: Pushed counters: nv_switch_util{board="rack18"} ~0.88, pcie_host_dma_bytes{node=~"r18.*"} high, tenant_kv_miss_ratio{tenant="t-orchid"} ~0.62, tenant_kv_miss_ratio{tenant="t-mistral"} ~0.59. Looks like a mix.
Eleni: If it's NVSwitch-heavy, routing across racks won't help. But if host DMA dominates, maybe NIC egress shaping can reduce host-initiated DMA bursts.
Sanjay: New idea: segmentation by PCIe domain + soft-fence NVSwitch lanes. Create a small reserved NVSwitch window for noisy tenants so they don't trample shared paths. Soft-fence = scheduler-level reservation rather than full carveout.
Kofi: Interesting. How would soft-fence work in practice? Reserve X% of NVSwitch fabric and enforce via kernel QoS + runtime scheduler?
Sanjay: Sketch: (1) detect offending tenant via combined signal: nv_switch_util > 0.8 && pcie_host_dma_rate > threshold && tenant_kv_miss_ratio > 0.55 for 2m; (2) label tenant with `fabric_softfence=true`; (3) runtime scheduler applies NVSwitch lane reservation and reduces host DMA burst allowance for that tenant for 60s; (4) monitor 10m; escalate to ephemeral carveout if sustained.
Noah: Prototype telemetry rule I used in staging (Prom style):
```
- alert: FabricPressureNoisyTenant
  expr: avg_over_time(nv_switch_util{board="rack18"}[3m]) > 0.8 and avg_over_time(pcie_host_dma_rate[3m]) > 1e7 and avg_over_time(tenant_kv_miss_ratio[3m]) > 0.55
  for: 2m
```
Priya: Before auto-enforcement, run dry-run for 72h and collect false positive rate. We must avoid catching warmups or model rollout activity.
Eleni: For the soft-fence enforcement layer, we can implement a scheduler token lease: each tenant gets `fabric_tokens` consumed on cross-GPU fetches. If they exceed their short-window allowance, we apply backpressure on KV fetches and optionally route to a low-kv variant.
Kofi: That token system sounds neat. Does it require kernel changes? Or can we implement in sidecar/runtime?
Sanjay: Prefer runtime-sidecar first (no kernel changes). Sidecar intercepts KV fetch paths and enforces token depletion, returning slow-path responses. Kernel/K8s-level NIC shaping is future work.
Noah: Quick sidecar policer example I used in staging:
```
curl -X POST https://runtime-api.internal/tenants/t-orchid/actions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"action":"fabric_softfence","tokens_per_min":1200,"burst":300,"duration_s":60}'
```
Eleni: Also propose a fallback routing rule: if tenant_label=fabric_softfence -> prefer `gen-kv-lite` variant. That reduces cross-GPU fetches while we mitigate.
Priya: What about cost/ops impact? Soft-fence avoids provisioning dedicated GPUs but adds scheduler complexity. If we escalate to ephemeral carveout, we need finance-friendly trial billing. Suggest marking carveouts as `trial:7d` so we don't auto-bill the customer until CS confirms.
Kofi: Agreed. Finance needs chargeability metadata. Add fields: `carveout_trial_days`, `charge_after_approve`. Ops should also add an audit trail entry for every soft-fence action.
Sanjay: Draft playbook (short):
1) Detect: fabric pressure rule fires (dry-run flag)
2) Dry-tag: apply `nvfabric_probe=true` (audit-only) for 72h to collect hits
3) Soft-fence (FF on): apply token lease + sidecar throttling for 60s windows, ramping if needed.
4) If sustained > 15m or repeated 3 times -> propose ephemeral 8x-A100 carveout with NVSwitch reservation + prewarm. Tag carveout as trial.
5) If soft-fence fails to recover -> route to `gen-kv-lite` and notify CS for customer outreach.
Noah: I ran a quick canary: applied token lease to t-orchid in staging, fabrics util dropped from 0.9 to 0.56 and 95p latency recovered. No client-visible errors in canary but saw small quality delta when fallback variant was used.
Priya: Action items:
- Noah: run 72h dry-run of the fabric rule in prod (dry-run only) and collect FP/TP stats (ETA: now)
- SAnjay: implement sidecar token lease prototype and PR behind FF (ETA: 48h)
- Kofi: coordinate finance for carveout-trial billing metadata (ETA: EOD)
- Eleni: spec routing fallback and measure quality deltas for top-3 models (ETA: 48h)
ops-bot: Incident INC-20260402-5 created; paging rotation notified. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/fabric-softfence
Kofi: One more ask: surface `fabric_softfence` events in billing dashboard so sales can proactively offer trials. Also keep a per-tenant `fabric_mitigation_history` for postmortems.
Noah: I'll post dry-run summary in #eng-infra in 72h. If dry-run shows many FPs we'll tighten thresholds. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
